items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity is high for fleet-wide go-live, new public exposure, and security-sensitive releases; ordinary reversible growth may continue conditionally when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence: the security fleet-doctor baseline is not OK with no run, checks, findings, or site results; operations has no deploy, uptime, or error-sweep results; and authentication/access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are unevidenced. Compliance is technical-only: 35 pass, 20 fail, 6 unknown. Recommendation: preserve private-launch and security-sensitive release gates, do not claim clearance or certification, and continue only the existing read-only evidence matrix.

Security gate: keep scaffold work preview-only. Do not publish, deploy, add credentials, permissions, dependencies, tracking, data collection, domains, or cross-site behavior until dated security evidence and normal legal, compliance, measurement, rollback, and owner gates are complete.

items.title: Maintain evidence-needed fleet security disposition and private release gates
items.summary: Fleet-wide security clearance is unsupported because fleet-doctor and operations results are absent and material controls remain unevidenced. Preserve private-launch and security-sensitive release gates while allowing only constrained reversible growth.
items.requested_action: Continue the existing consolidated read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Document authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, incident response readiness, and security.txt or disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, request duplicate telemetry, conduct external outreach, or claim certification.
